raw_response:
I farm only 3 mu, so every bag of fertilizer matters. I will do almost the same as last year, with small adjustments from what I saw in the village. Around me, if wheat gets too little bottom fertilizer, the heads stay small, and if maize is short of fertilizer at jointing, the ears do not fill well. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose grain. Since I have well irrigation, I will keep the wheat steadier with more water and give maize fewer irrigations because summer rain usually helps. For seed, I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because people here have used them for years and I have seen the yield. On my small land, I will still rely mostly on family labor, so I will keep the plan simple: rotary tillage after each harvest, enough base fertilizer, one topdressing for each crop, and pesticide only when the main problem shows up.

decision.reasoning_summary: I will follow the usual wheat-maize cycle on all 3 mu because that is what has worked for me for many years. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed since I have seen good results from my own fields and neighbors' fields. I will put enough nitrogen first because I do not want to risk low yield, and I will add phosphorus and potassium too so the crop stands stronger and fills grain better. Wheat will get more irrigation because I have well water and wheat here responds clearly to watering, while maize will get fewer irrigations because summer rain can help. I will keep rotary tillage for convenience on my small farm and do two pesticide sprays on each crop to handle the common field problems without overspending.
